thesis_triggers.event: Reviewed 2026-10-23 after the Oct 22 Q3 print (kept at $150): at ~$150 BE would trade at ~29x the build's horizon NTM GAAP EPS (~$5.12) with FY2026 revenue already raised to $4.4-4.6B, which only makes sense with real cuts to product_gw or product_gm. $150 is 22% below the $193.30 close of 2026-10-23 and below the $163.75 post-Q2 close of 2026-07-29 (src 27), and ~28x the post-print FY2027 consensus EPS of $5.31 (src 25), with net debt near zero ($16.2M, converts carried as debt). That only makes sense with real estimate cuts: FERC denying or courts blocking the rerouted Green Chile lateral, or the air permit being denied rather than extended, with no redeployment of the 2.4 GW; a Feb 2027 FY27 guide well below ~$7B revenue; gross margin under ~30%; a scandium supply disruption; or an AI-capex pullback. A permit-deadline extension or a pipeline slip of a few months is not a thesis break.

supervisor_summary: In the base round (2026-09-25) the five revised forecasts clustered tightly: research targets $222-245 (mean ~$235) and P(>= spot) 0.46-0.49. The one contested fact checks out but is less damaging than it sounds. New Mexico did deny the Jupiter pipeline's state-land crossing twice (Mar 20 and Jul 14), but the denial covers ~0.63 miles, and the rerouted lateral is under FERC review with a Dec 3 decision. Separately, the air-permit hearing has not yet been held, so the Nov 23 deadline will probably be extended. I nudge the middle of the ladder down ~0.5pt for a likelier slip of Jupiter revenue into 2028; confidence is low, and the forecast stays near the mean with a median just below spot. The driver-led build of 2026-10-23 sets the research target (12m) at $185.84, below the $193.30 close.
